thread:
marta: alert - sudden spike in 5xx from eu-central-1 for inference-api, noise started ~02:11 UTC, current 5xx ~11% (normal <0.5%). ELB logs show many 502/504.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED · ID INC-1747654321 · severity: P1 · channel: #incidents · pager: @ryan (oncall)
ryan: ack. joining bridge. pulling ELB target health + instance metrics for eu-central-1. can someone confirm if this is isolated to a single AZ? :mag_right:
kai: initial look — heavy EBS attach/describe latency in eu-central-1 AZ-b. We're seeing AttachVolume timeouts and EC2 API 5xx/504s. kubelet on nodes hits container start failures -> ELB target unhealthy churn.
marta: quick curl to the app VIP returns 502 within app timeout window:
```bash
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://inference.redwood.example/v1/health
502 0.147
```
ryan: describe-target-health (elbv2) shows many targets UNHEALTHY with reason: "target response code: 502"; most affected targets in eu-central-1 AZ-b. ASG logs show frequent detach/attach cycles.
kai: digging into EC2 API call traces — a pattern emerges: EBS controller errors and delayed attach confirmations. Could be control-plane saturation in that AZ. Opening AWS support case now.
incident-bot: AWS SUPPORT CASE OPENED · case: 9876543210 · severity: investigatory P1
support-ops: prepping customer comms. initial blast radius estimate: ~20% of traffic hitting eu-central-1 (global), 120 customers with active traffic there. Drafting status page banner.
ryan: mitigation options: 1) shift weighted DNS away from eu-central-1 to reduce incoming load 2) adjust ELB health thresholds to avoid flapping while drains complete 3) cordon/drain noisy AZ-b nodes to stop attach churn 4) suspend ASG scale-in in eu-central until AWS confirms control plane stability. Thoughts?
marta: agree with that plan. also want to snapshot logs for postmortem: ELB access logs, kubelet, and kernel dmesg around attach timeouts.
kai: applying Route53 weight change to bias traffic to eu-west-2 (closer region, low latency):
```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z0EXAMPLE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-2","Weight":80}}]}'
```
kai: update: change applied. new weights: eu-west-2=80, eu-central-1=20. watching.
marta: CloudWatch: within 6 minutes of the weight change, eu-central-1 5xx dropped from 11% -> 4.5%, global 5xx down overall. but ELB target churn persists in AZ-b.
ryan: adjusting ELB target-group healthcheck and deregistration delay to reduce noisy failovers:
```bash
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-inference/abcd1234 --health-check-interval-seconds 15 --health-check-timeout-seconds 10 --healthy-threshold-count 5 --unhealthy-threshold-count 4 --deregistration-delay-seconds 300
```
ryan: applied. this should reduce rapid re-registration.
kai: AWS replied on case: internal control plane issue in eu-central-1 (AZ-b) impacting EBS attach and instance lifecycle APIs. They are implementing control-plane throttling mitigation; ETA unknown. Case updated.
support-ops: posted status banner: "We are experiencing elevated errors in eu-central-1 affecting inference requests. Traffic is being shifted to eu-west-2 while we work with AWS. No customer data loss identified. Updates every 30 minutes."
oncall: we need to decide handoff cadence — I'll be available for 45 more minutes, then handoff to night oncall @lena. Leave all mitigation state in thread.
lena: ack, will take over at T+45. please list checks and outstanding blockers before handoff.
ryan: checklist for handoff (log these verbatim):
- Route53 weights: eu-west-2=80, eu-central-1=20
- ELB target-group healthcheck changed and deregistration-delay=300
- ASG scale-in suspended in eu-central-1
- AWS support case 9876543210 open and being monitored
- Customer status banner posted
- Logs archived to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-1747654321/

kai: performing node cordon & drain on AZ-b noisy nodes to stop attach churn. example commands used:
```bash
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-23-45
kubectl drain ip-10-0-23-45 --ignore-daemonsets --force --delete-local-data
```
kai: drain in progress; pods rescheduled to eu-central-1c and eu-west-2 replicas. this should reduce attach pressure.
incident-bot: PAGERDUTY ESCALATION: SRE manager @suresh notified.
support-ops: CS notified and prepared customer-facing remediation suggestions (move traffic, retry policies). Preparing postmortem template and assigning owner.
marta: log snapshot link uploaded to bridge. timestamps show EBS attach timeouts peaking at 02:14:22 UTC with many 30s+ attach latencies reported.
ryan: monitoring: eu-central-1 5xx now ~1.8%. global back to baseline for the moment. leaving Route53 weights in place for two hours and reassess.
lena: joining bridge early. I have the runbook and docs. I'll take over monitoring and will escalate if AWS posts broader region notice.
oncall: adding outstanding actions for handoff: 1) confirm ASG can be resumed when AWS confirms attach latencies normalize 2) obtain AWS RCA and any suggested compensations 3) prepare internal blameless summary and customer follow-up once RCA received
marta: I'll own postmortem and follow up with AWS on RCA. tagging @suresh for internal review once we have timelines.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED · severity: P1 -> P2 (mitigated traffic shift in place) · last-updated-by: ryan
ryan: prepping short internal summary and will handoff notes to @lena. leaving detailed timeline + commands + links to logs in the incident doc.
lena: acknowledged. I'll continue monitoring and update the status page if anything changes. planning to close incident when eu-central 5xx <1% for 30m and ASG resumed safely.
support-ops: draft customer follow-up ready; will hold final message until AWS RCA included. marking incident as 'mitigated' on status page.
marta: closing notes: postmortem owner assigned (marta). AWS case id 9876543210. keep archived logs & config diffs in the incident S3 folder.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED · mitigation: weighted DNS shift + node drains + ELB config change · closed at 1747658800
